findings.reason: the author must either extend `_plan_declarations` (or the owner) to resolve record ids from the file too, or state that the inventory row always carries `sections`; as written the record-only arm of §15's done-when cannot be met at an inventory-row caller.
findings.text: §15 states that a caller holding only an inventory row "feeds the owner the file-aware declarations the roadmap already resolves (`_plan_declarations`, `roadmap.py:128`)", but `_plan_declarations` reads only `read_state(text)["section_declarations"]` from the file and never the typed section records (`sections`); at the roadmap ref-validation sites (`roadmap.py:831`, `:947`, `:2470`) the target comes from `all_plans`, whose rows (`roadmap.py:2240`) may carry neither `section_declarations` nor `sections`, so the plan's own done-when arm — "another whose only evidence is a typed record … each roadmap staged-ref site reports `section_found` true" — is unmet for such a row: the owner receives a set that omits the record-only section and reports it absent

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the section adds no module and no definition; it routes four existing ref-validation sites and two existence-asking sites onto one existing function, so the surface it touches shrinks rather than grows.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the section retires the duplicate owner `_declared_stages` (`reckon/roadmap.py:181`) and moves every existence check onto `declared_section_identities`; the census of `plan_section_anchors` callers is complete (`_schema.py:589`, `roadmap.py:831`, `:947`, `:2470`, `:2990`, `:189` inside the retired helper, `:233` via its fallback, `promotion.py:7273`; `_schema.py:692` is the owner calling itself and `promotion.py` and `_schema.py:754`'s narrower anchor meaning is correctly retained).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1523, cli_options 323, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §15 adds to none of the four and states in its own text what it retires ("no definition added, one private duplicate (`_declared_stages`) retired, and the identifier grammar applied uniformly"), which satisfies the account-or-justify rule.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §15 searched `reckon/` and names the existing owner it extends (`declared_section_identities`, `reckon/_schema.py:678`) and the duplicate it retires (`_declared_stages`, `reckon/roadmap.py:181`), adding no new machinery of its own — but its file-aware fallback for inventory rows is incomplete (finding below).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is added; §15 changes callers to call the existing owner, which is the extension the item asks for, not a parallel layer over it.
